```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(rtracklayer)

project_root <- normalizePath(path.expand(params$project_root), mustWork = TRUE)
datasets <- unique(as.character(unlist(params$datasets, use.names = FALSE)))
source(file.path(project_root, "R", "validation.R"))
source(file.path(project_root, "scripts", "PCHiC_enrichment.R"))
source(file.path(project_root, "R", "validation_plots.R"))

method_levels <- validation_method_levels
```

This report compares significant peak--gene associations with promoter capture
Hi-C (PCHiC) interactions from Javierre et al. (Cell, 2016; DATA S1). It uses
the PCHiC other-end fragment as the candidate regulatory interval, lifts hg19
coordinates to hg38, requires a matching `baitName`, and evaluates enrichment
with a one-sided Fisher exact test.

The scMultiMap manuscript's PBMC analysis used the `Mon` PCHiC column for CD14
monocytes and adjusted (p < 0.1). This report additionally maps the broad
EpiLink groups as follows so all available groups can be inspected; these broad
comparisons are extensions of, rather than exact replications of, the published
CD14-monocyte analysis.

```{r mapping}
mapping_table <- bind_rows(lapply(names(default_pchic_celltype_map), function(celltype) {
  data.frame(celltype = celltype,
             PCHiC_columns = paste(default_pchic_celltype_map[[celltype]], collapse = ", "))
}))
kable(mapping_table)
```

`Tnk` has no exact reference match because the PCHiC matrix has T-cell but no
NK-cell column. Foetal thymus (`FoeT`) is intentionally excluded. `Myeloid` is
compared with monocytes (`Mon`), matching the scMultiMap paper; `Bcell` uses
naive and total B-cell columns.

## Read PCHiC validation sets

```{r read-pchic}
references <- load_pchic_reference(
  project_root,
  chicago_cutoff = params$chicago_cutoff,
  chicago_operator = params$chicago_operator,
  expand_multigene_baits = params$expand_multigene_baits
)

reference_summary <- data.frame(
  celltype = names(references),
  significant_lifted_interactions = vapply(references, length, integer(1L)),
  unique_bait_names = vapply(references, function(x) length(unique(x$gene)), integer(1L))
)
kable(reference_summary)
```

The published code comments describe CHiCAGO score \(\ge 5\), but both the
scMultiMap manuscript notebook and package vignette implement `score > 5`.
The default above follows the executable code. Set `chicago_operator: ">="` to
follow the prose literally. Exact `baitName` matching also follows their code;
set `expand_multigene_baits: true` to split semicolon-delimited bait annotations.

## Compute enrichment

All methods use the complete EpiLink-Poisson tested pair set for their cell type
as a common universe. As in scMultiMap's procedure, that universe is restricted
to genes represented among significant PCHiC bait names. A tested pair is a
PCHiC positive when its peak overlaps a significant other-end fragment and its
gene exactly matches the corresponding bait name. Duplicate interval hits are
collapsed to one binary status per tested pair before constructing the 2-by-2
table.

```{r compute}
metric_list <- lapply(datasets, function(dataset) {
  metrics <- compute_dataset_pchic(
    project_root, dataset, references,
    allow_missing = isTRUE(params$partial),
    correction = isTRUE(params$correction)
  )
  output_dir <- file.path(project_root, "results", "real", dataset,
                          "validation", "PCHiC",
                          if (isTRUE(params$correction)) "correction_T" else "correction_F")
  dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  fwrite(metrics, file.path(output_dir, "enrichment_metrics.tsv"), sep = "\t")
  metrics
})
metrics <- bind_rows(metric_list)
metrics$method <- factor(metrics$method, levels = method_levels)
metrics$cutoff_label <- factor(
  paste0("FDR = ", metrics$cutoff),
  levels = paste0("FDR = ", sort(unique(metrics$cutoff)))
)

metrics %>%
  select(dataset, celltype, method, cutoff, TP, FP, FN, TN, odds_ratio,
         CI_low, CI_high, pval, n_universe, n_selected, n_pchic_links) %>%
  arrange(dataset, celltype, cutoff, method) %>%
  kable(digits = 3)
```

## Canonical odds-ratio figures

The report writes exactly two PDFs per dataset. The first contains four
cell-type panels (including pooled `All`) with odds-ratio trajectories over FDR
cutoffs. The second contains the corresponding 4-by-4 odds-ratio/95% CI grid.

```{r odds-ratio, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
for (dataset in datasets) {
  dataset_metrics <- metrics[metrics$dataset == dataset, , drop = FALSE]
  dataset_metrics <- append_validation_all(dataset_metrics)
  figure_dir <- file.path(project_root, "results", "real", dataset,
                          "validation", "figures")
  dir.create(figure_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  p_or <- plot_validation_odds_ratio(dataset_metrics, dataset, "PCHiC")
  suffix <- if (isTRUE(params$correction)) "T" else "F"
  ggsave(file.path(figure_dir, paste0("odds_ratio_pchic_correction_", suffix, ".pdf")), p_or,
         width = 12, height = 8)
  print(p_or)
}
```
